the sequences encoding four of the five major virus glycoprotein species (VP8.0, VP7, VP8.5, and VP19E) map in the L component.

the HSV genome encodes at least four major glycoproteinstwo of which are specified in two locations in HSV DNA and that the HSV genome contains at least three loci specifying the clumping of infected cells.

the sequences encoding four of the major glycoprotein components of herpesvirus are located in the HSV genome and that the social behavior of the cells infected with the virus is controlled by at least three different genetic loci.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics of HSV-1 and -2.
the genetic control of the social behavior of HSV-infected cells.
the genetic control of the synthesis of HSV structural proteins and with the molecular basis of the differences between HSV strains in the social behavior of the cells they infect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sequences encoding four of the major glycoproteines of HSV-1 map in two regions of HSV DNA, and that three loci determine the social behavior of HSV-infected cells.
the HSV-1 DNA contains three loci (syn 1, syn 2, and syn 3) determining the social behavior of the infected cells, and that the HSV-2 DNA contains a fourth locus (syn 4).
the HSV genome contains at least four loci determining the social behavior of the infected cell, and that these loci are distinct from the Cr and VP8.0 loci.

the HSV DNA is organized such that the sequences encoding glycoproteins map to different regions and that there are at least three loci specifying the ability of cells to form syncytia.
